text:
Noah Cates is the kind of player whose value lives off the scoresheet, and Evolving-Hockey said so loudly last season: 2.1 wins above replacement, 47th among 401 forwards, with most of it from the penalty kill and opponents getting 0.19 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on (97th percentile).

This season the scoresheet is thin. Five points in 22 games after 47 last season, and his own chance rate has dropped from 0.92 individual expected goals per 60 to 0.55. Some of it is luck, since the Flyers have scored about three goals fewer than their chances with him on, but most of it is fewer looks.

The defensive work hasn't gone anywhere. Philadelphia takes 52% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, more than ten points better than without him, which makes him one of the few Flyers forwards actually tilting the ice. He plays like Justin Hryckowian and Jamie Benn: dumps it in, gets to the net, keeps the other team quiet. On a team searching for answers late in games, he's one of the reliable ones. We'd watch whether the points catch up to the play.
